sentences.text: Researchers developed a computational system that integrates two distinct artificial intelligence methods to distinguish between two types of brain tumors using T2-weighted and contrast-enhanced T1-weighted MRI scans.

The model was evaluated on 344 patients with biopsy-confirmed diagnoses and subsequently validated on an external cohort from different hospitals, where an automated tool outlined tumor regions that were manually corrected by experts.

This combined approach correctly identified tumor types in 95.4% of the primary group and 90.9% of the external validation group, outperforming individual AI techniques with the largest gains observed in the new patient population.
Analysis indicated that relying solely on these two specific MRI sequences yielded optimal performance, as incorporating additional imaging types did not enhance the system's accuracy.
The authors conclude that merging different AI techniques may assist clinicians in classifying brain tumors via MRI without requiring a biopsy, thereby supporting medical decision-making.
